cards.title: ACSM: Resistance Training Prescription (2026)
cards.tags: strength hypertrophy frequency volume сила м’язи гіпертрофія обсяг частота план
cards.summary: An overview of 137 reviews found that progressive resistance training improves strength and muscle size. Heavier loads favored maximal strength. Higher weekly volume favored hypertrophy; volume-equated frequency comparisons did not establish a universal hypertrophy advantage. Failure training and periodization were not consistently superior. Individual prescription still depends on goals and tolerance.
cards.limitations: Group averages, heterogeneous studies; not an individualized kilogram prescription or evidence that any branded routine is best. A weekly volume association is not a mandatory minimum for every individual.

cards.title: Hickmott et al.: Load and Volume Autoregulation (2022)
cards.tags: autoregulation RIR RPE fatigue progression авторегуляція втома прогрес запас
cards.summary: Autoregulated and standardized load prescription produced similar strength improvements. Velocity-loss comparisons suggested trade-offs between fatigue, strength and hypertrophy. Effort feedback can support individual adjustment, but autoregulation is not proven universally superior.
cards.limitations: Small evidence base for some comparisons. Velocity measurements are not interchangeable with subjective RIR. Does not validate an AI coach or a fixed percentage reduction after illness.

cards.title: Robinson et al.: Proximity to Failure Meta-Regressions (2024)
cards.population: Resistance-training studies with estimated repetitions in reserve
cards.tags: failure RIR strength hypertrophy відмова запас повторення м’язи сила
cards.summary: The relationship between proximity to failure and adaptation differed for strength and hypertrophy. Hypertrophy was more meaningfully related to estimated RIR than strength was.
cards.limitations: RIR was estimated from study descriptions. Associations do not establish an exact optimal RIR for this user or require every set to failure.

cards.title: Refalo et al.: Failure versus Repetitions in Reserve (2024)
cards.population: Resistance-trained participants; eight weeks; quadriceps outcomes
cards.tags: failure RIR hypertrophy fatigue відмова втома гіпертрофія запас
cards.summary: Stopping close to failure, around one or two repetitions in reserve, produced similar quadriceps hypertrophy to momentary failure in this eight-week comparison.
cards.limitations: Short duration and muscle-specific findings; do not generalize to all exercises, all trainees or long-term outcomes.

cards.title: Schoenfeld et al.: Training Volume in Trained Men (2019)
cards.population: 34 resistance-trained men; one, three or five sets per exercise
cards.tags: volume hypertrophy strength trained обсяг підходи досвід м’язи сила
cards.summary: Strength improved without significant between-group differences. Some measured hypertrophy outcomes favored greater training volume.
cards.limitations: Small male sample and limited study duration; more volume is not always better and the study does not prescribe a personal recoverable volume.

cards.title: Currier et al.: Resistance Training Prescription Network Meta-analysis (2023)
cards.kind: systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis
cards.tags: frequency sets load program strength hypertrophy частота вага програма сила м’язи
cards.summary: Across the analyzed prescriptions, resistance training improved strength and hypertrophy compared with no exercise. Different combinations of load, sets and frequency were compared.
cards.limitations: Network rankings are not a personalized ranking of branded programs. Results cannot supply exact weights from body measurements.

cards.title: Mayo Clinic: Exercise and illness
cards.kind: clinical patient guidance, not a training trial
cards.tags: illness fever return recovery sick хвороба хворію температура одужав біль відновлення пропуск
cards.summary: Do not exercise with fever, fatigue or widespread muscle aches. Illness can justify reduced intensity and duration or rest. Return gradually as you feel better; seek clinical advice when uncertain.
cards.limitations: Does not provide an exact post-illness percentage prescription. A language model cannot diagnose illness or provide medical clearance.
